content.comment_body: Hello, I'm new to [product_name] and want to convert my home lighting from impulse relays to [product_name]. My first project has the N connected to the push buttons instead of the L, and the N is sent to the input of [product_name]. 1. Will this setup function, or will [product_name] compare the N on the input to the N on its power connection, which would always result in 0V? 2. If not, is it possible to swap L1 and N at the power input so the N at the input can be compared with the L1 at the N terminal of [product_name]? I hope my question isn't too confusing!
Yes, you can swap the phase and neutral connections. I've done this several times before.
Thank you for your reply. I received my first [product_name] last week, tested it, and can confirm that it works as intended.
It is technically possible, but not recommended. If you're not careful, the phase might end up connected to an input, which could cause damage.

I've tried this myself with a 230V input; nothing happens, and there are no other problems. My theory is that it simply measures the potential difference between F and N, so connecting N to N means there's no potential difference.
That's straightforward. A voltage difference can only be detected between L and N—not between N and N.

analysis.insight_summary: Users discussed proper wiring for inputs on a 230V [product_name] module for home lighting automation. The main concern was whether neutral (N) can be safely connected to push-buttons and to the module inputs, and the impact of swapping line (L) and neutral (N) at the power connection. Responses confirmed how the module processes voltage differences and provided safety recommendations, highlighting the need for clearer beginner wiring guidance.
analysis.user_expectations: The user seeks reliable information about connecting neutral (N) to both push-buttons and [product_name] inputs, and whether swapping line (L) and neutral (N) is safe and effective for wiring. Guidance focused on both operational safety and functional performance is expected.
